findings.reason: it changes where the fix lands (in `dispatch()`, keyed on the node id, or adding `queue_admission.py` to the write paths and a second done-when case for a queued review), and a node that follows the named caller alone ships a partial fix on a real production path.
findings.text: §34 names a single caller "A composed plan review reaches dispatch() through reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py", but a plan review composed while the lane holds is queued and later launched by the admission pass through `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:874`/`:295` → `_launch_queued` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:157,172-190`), which calls `dispatch()` with the recorded `plan-review-of-<slug>` node and no first-attempt marker; a fix made only at the named call site leaves the queued relaunch recording `redispatch` at a climbing attempt, and the done-when's test (two reviews in a temporary home) cannot detect it — so "the distinction is made at that call" under-specifies where the change must land, and the write-path list omits `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `PLAN_REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX`, the node-id composition in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:589`, `dispatch()` in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:708`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`, and `PLAN_REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX` all resolve; `attempt-34-worker.json` matches the real per-attempt name those two run dirs hold (`attempt-35-worker.json`), built at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1566`; the calibration discard rule resolves at `reckon/calibration.py:126` (`attempt > 1` and a wall/missing source → `untrustworthy_duration`) and the picker's `attempts` field at `reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:422`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §34's done-when is measurable (two content reviews in a temporary home, the second at attempt 1/`dispatch`; an implementation node re-dispatched at attempt 2/`redispatch`) and it declares a negative control ("with the composed review dispatched as before, the second review records attempt 2 and kind redispatch, and the test fails; the control is logged under the run directory"), so the gate can show the guard fires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the control is logged under the crew run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`), the test lives in `tests/`, and no gate writes to a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test path `tests/test_a_new_plan_review_is_a_first_attempt.py` reads as a mechanism, and §34 introduces no plan label, ticket number or version tag and no changelog prose into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the cited evidence and reproduces live (see below), but §34 names only `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` as the caller that reaches `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, while a queued plan review is relaunched by the admission pass through `queue_admission._launch_queued`, which calls `dispatch()` directly.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 carries one deliverable (composed plan reviews are dispatching-first attempts), with the implementation-node case as the contrast that bounds the change rather than a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §34 declares no `depends-on`/`informs`/`gates` and needs none: it changes attempt accounting inside `dispatch()` and its one composer, and no other unit gates on or is gated by it, so nothing is missing and nothing points at the wrong node.
